about: Code rules the build applies to the model's devices on its first run (bim.coderules), and Validate checks again. Each rule: its id, the code section, what it sets, and where it applies. Validate's E-RECEPT-TYPE / E-RECEPT-TR prescreen and its G-PRODUCT-CODE rule (TR, GFCI by circuit, WR outdoors) read the same file. The lighting step reads E-LIGHT-OCC (the energy code's occupant-sensor spaces and a guest room's master control).

rules.rule: Every 125/250 V, 15 and 20 A receptacle in a guest room or guest suite of a hotel or motel, and in a dwelling unit, is tamper-resistant (GFCI receptacles included).

GFCI protection is judged per circuit: the rule only adds the protection the code requires and never removes protection the drawings call for. A receptacle the drawings show standard on a GFCI (or dual-function) breaker is already protected and stays standard; where the print tags GFCI or the place needs it and the breaker isn't GFCI, the first device on the circuit is a GFCI receptacle and the ones after it on its load side are standard. A receptacle the drawings tag GFCI on a GFCI breaker stays a GFCI device: redundant protection is allowed, reported as information for value engineering. When the breaker's type isn't known the decision is left undecided.
rules.location_rule: A receptacle the print doesn't tag GFCI needs it within 6 ft of the outside edge of a sink (NEC 210.8(A)(7), (B)(5)), or in a place below (its circuit's description or its room's name has all of a place's words); it is decided by its circuit like a tagged one.

rules.rule: A 15 or 20 A, 125 or 250 V nonlocking receptacle in a damp or wet location (outdoors: an exterior wall, a roof, a balcony, a patio or deck) is a listed weather-resistant type. In our own words: verify with the authority having jurisdiction.

rules.large_equipment_cite: NEC 110.26(C)(2): equipment rated 1200 A or more and over 6 ft wide needs an entrance at each end of its working space (or double the depth)
rules.wireway_cite: NEC 376.22 (wireway fill), 312.5 (conductors entering enclosures); a wireway above an enclosure takes the raceways its plate can't
rules.rule: In front of electrical equipment likely to be worked on energized: a clear space as deep as the voltage to ground and the condition call for (0-150 V: 3 ft; 151-600 V: 3, 3.5 or 4 ft by condition 1, 2, 3), at least 30 in wide or the equipment's width, and 6.5 ft high. Gear the plans don't locate is laid out along its room's walls with that space clear (condition 1 assumed and said).

An equipment connection follows its approved submittal: its protection no larger than the maker's maximum (fuse class as named), its conductors' ampacity at least 125% of its nameplate / full-load current (its minimum circuit amps when given), its controller's short-circuit current rating at least the available fault current where it is installed. Where the drawings differ, the build reports both values and the fix.
rules.disconnect_cite: NEC 430.110(A) (a motor's disconnect at least 115% of its full-load current), 440.12(A) (an air-conditioning unit's at least 115% of its rated-load or nameplate current), 620.51 (an elevator's: fused or circuit breaker, lockable open); standard switch sizes
rules.min_ocpd_cite: NEC 440.22(A) and 430.52 (the branch circuit's protection carries the unit's starting and running current: no smaller than its minimum circuit ampacity calls for), 240.4, 240.6(A) standard sizes
rules.conductor_cite: NEC 110.3(B) (listed equipment is installed by its instructions: the conductor material and least size its maker names), 110.14 (terminations rated for the conductor), 310.16
rules.sight_cite: NEC 440.14 (an air-conditioning unit's disconnecting means within sight of it and readily accessible), 430.102(B) (a motor's within sight), Article 100 (within sight: visible and not more than 50 ft)
rules.aux_cite: NEC 110.3(B) (the connections the listed unit's instructions call for), 210.63 (a 125 V service receptacle within 25 ft of heating, air-conditioning and refrigeration equipment, on its own circuit where the unit's outlet is fed apart); the data connection the maker's controls call for has a pathway (NEC 800, 725)

rules.rule: Lights in these spaces are controlled by an occupant sensor that turns them off soon after the space is left: classrooms, lecture and training rooms; conference, meeting and multipurpose rooms; copy and print rooms; lounges and break rooms; enclosed offices and open office areas; restrooms; storage rooms; locker rooms; warehouse storage. The starter list in our own words, section numbers by edition: verify with the authority having jurisdiction.

guest_rooms.rule: Each hotel or motel guest room (sleeping unit) has a master control that turns off its luminaires and switched receptacles within 20 minutes of the room being left: a card key or captive key switch, or an occupant sensor. In our own words: verify with the authority having jurisdiction.
